correctness.rationale: Full reconstruction checks the weighted arbitrary-mass tree induction with jointly concave extreme-point minimization, equality construction for the de Bruijn state rule, multinomial sum and square-root exponential tilt, aperiodic lattice local-limit with dominated summation, strict d-monotonicity and the deviation-matrix/oscillation hitting estimate. Every boundary is explicit: integer q>=3,d>=1 and 0<b<1/q. The independent finite checker passed 12,277 finite assertions; the proof, not enumerations, covers all depths and parameters. The sufficient hitting threshold is explicitly not elevated to a necessary hitting condition.

originality.rationale: The strongest close primary manuscript proves a sharp binary extremal overlap (Theorems 3-4), but its general finite-alphabet treatment supplies an unspecified block overlap or Hellinger-affinity surrogate (Theorem 24, Corollary 26). Here an all-q exact minimax multinomial formula, its aperiodic lazy-walk asymptotic constant, and the strictly stronger sufficient hitting regime are established. The older Doeblin work provides generic contraction tools without this categorical-window optimization. Semantic searches, source/alias comparisons and recovered historical claims found no directly covering implication, but priority is provisional and a missing classical equivalent remains a risk.
residual_risks: Classical adaptive categorical product-test inequalities or older de Bruijn chain results could contain an equivalent theorem under another name.
The full text of Alhakim 2004 was not inspected; the abstract alone is insufficient to rule out overlap.

value.rationale: The q-ary case is a natural extension of a current finite-memory learning and hitting-time program, and the exact worst-case block overlap supplies the missing quantity in a published arbitrary-alphabet theorem. New structural features include strictly decreasing overlaps rather than the binary parity plateaux and an aperiodic walk with an explicit sharp prefactor. The bound improves a generic affinity criterion on a nonempty parameter set (e.g. q=3,b=0.14). Its usefulness is not contingent on proving the unknown necessity threshold for actual hitting times.
